leading_positions.synthesis: Three members prefer palladium-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling with the identical two-laureate configuration (Buchwald and Hartwig). They share the view that maturity, independent confirmation and attribution are unusually clean. They differ on emphasis: Somfai stresses that recognition is overdue and that it is core chemistry, Chabes stresses that a two-name prize avoids forced omissions, and Aqvist stresses ligand-controlled mechanistic novelty over the 2010 cross-coupling prize. All three also name the 2010 overlap and the Kosugi (and, per Somfai and Chabes, Migita) precursor as open points. Their alternatives differ: B026 and B004 (Aqvist), B037 and B026 (Chabes), B033 and B026 (Somfai). Zou, Brzezinski and Sparr list B065 as an alternative, and I list it as my first alternative, but these are not preferred configurations.

Two members prefer targeted protein degradation as a new event-driven pharmacological modality, with Crews and Deshaies as the shared core. They differ on the third laureate: Aili names Ciulli (structure-guided VHL ligands, rational design), Brzezinski names Handa (cereblon as the thalidomide target, anchoring the glue strand). Both accept that the other choice is defensible and that no PROTAC drug is yet approved. B026 is a listed alternative for Linke, Sparr and Zou (and for Aqvist, Chabes and Somfai), but only Aili and Brzezinski place it in their preferred configuration.

I (chair) prefer massively parallel sequencing with a two-laureate Solexa configuration (Balasubramanian and Klenerman), narrowed from my opening three names after Chabes argued against adding Mayer. Chabes lists B037 as an alternative and agrees on the two-name core, but he also questions whether it is chemistry or genomics technology, a concern shared by Somfai, Aili, Brzezinski, Aqvist and Sparr in varying forms. No other member prefers it.

One member prefers ionizable lipid nanoparticles with the Vancouver trio (Cullis, Hope, Madden) as defined by lipid and formulation principles. Brzezinski would hold it as a second-part candidate or alternative but does not prefer it as lead. Contested credit (Anderson and Langer lipidoids, MacLachlan, industrial developers) and the 2023 Medicine prize remain open.

One member prefers halide perovskite solar absorbers with Miyasaka, Park and Snaith as a new materials class. Aqvist and Somfai explicitly would wait on stability and toxicity, and both note that credit is spread over at least six names. Zou states that she does not claim majority support.

areas_of_agreement: No candidate is supported by a majority of five as the preferred configuration in round 1: the explicit preferences split three (B065), two (B026), and one each for B037, B045 and B056, so round 2 must narrow the field.
Members that prefer B065 give the same two-laureate allocation, and no member disputes that Buchwald and Hartwig are the core of that discovery or that it is mature and widely confirmed.

B026 appears in all eight members' round-1 files, as a preferred configuration for Aili and Brzezinski and as a listed alternative for the other six, and its concept and independent mechanistic confirmation are not disputed; the objections concern maturity and allocation.
Members broadly agree that a three-name cap forces hard omissions on most candidates, and that cleaner two-name allocations are easier to defend.

Several members agree the impact of massively parallel sequencing is exceptional and its Solexa core (Balasubramanian, Klenerman) is the most defensible allocation; the disagreement is about chemistry classification and extra names.
scientific_disputes: Whether Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling is a new conceptual advance (amide-bound palladium intermediates, difficult reductive elimination, ligand-controlled mechanism, per Aqvist) or a downstream extension of the 2010 C-C cross-coupling prize (per Aili, Brzezinski, Sparr, and Aqvist and Chabes as self-identified counterarguments).

Whether massively parallel sequencing is chemistry (reversible terminators, surface chemistry, single-molecule detection, per Linke) or genomics and platform engineering (raised by Somfai, Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski, Sparr).
Whether lipid nanoparticle delivery rests on lipid physical chemistry (Sparr, Brzezinski) or is better read as pharmaceutics and medicine.

Whether protein degradation by PROTACs and by cereblon-based molecular glues is one discovery or two distinct strands that a single citation would blur (Aili, Aqvist, Chabes, Somfai, Sparr and Zou each raise this in some form).

Whether halide perovskites are a new functional materials class whose scientific case does not depend on commercialization (Zou) or whether stability and lead toxicity make the case incomplete (Aqvist, Somfai).
attribution_disputes: B065: whether Kosugi (and Migita) should be reflected in laureates, or only in citation wording such as 'general catalytic' (Aqvist, Chabes, Somfai, Zou); ligand-generation credit is also called contestable.
B026: third laureate Ciulli (Aili) versus Handa (Brzezinski), with Ito, Gray, Kim and Sakamoto outside any three-name set; Zou suggests a two-part PROTAC and glue structure.

B037: Balasubramanian and Klenerman only (Linke now, Chabes) versus adding Mayer (my opening trio, Sparr's description), with Rothberg and Ju as parallel-route claimants and Aili's view that all of Rothberg, Ju and Mayer have credible claims.
B045: the Vancouver trio (Cullis, Hope, Madden) versus the Anderson and Langer lipidoid line and MacLachlan.
B056: which three of Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Seok, Gratzel and Kanatzidis, and how to treat Kojima, who is not among the credited names.

Whether any alternative shortlist candidates (B004 base editing with Liu alone versus trainees plus Kondo and Nishida; B033 photoredox without MacMillan) can be attributed more cleanly than the leading positions.
maturity_disputes: B026: no PROTAC drug is yet approved, so Aqvist, Chabes, Somfai, Sparr and I regard recognition as early, while Aili, Brzezinski and Zou treat the mechanisms as independently confirmed enough.
B056: stability, toxicity and commercialization are unresolved (Aqvist, Somfai, Zou herself acknowledges this).
B004: the 2020 CRISPR prize and the still-emerging clinical record (Somfai, Aili, Chabes).
B037, B065 and B045 are described as mature by their proponents, and the dispute is about category and attribution rather than time since discovery.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Linke (chair): preferred B037 and was first-place on it at opening; he states he will take care not to let that steer discussion. No documented tie to Balasubramanian, Klenerman or others.
Chabes: heavy daily user of massively parallel sequencing (B037, his alternative), self-flagged as a possible over-weighting of its importance; no recusal needed.
Sparr: research field of lipid self-assembly is adjacent to B045, her preferred candidate, and she shares a Lund affiliation with Linke and Somfai; no recusal judged necessary.
Somfai: works in synthetic methodology, the field of B065 and B033; no direct tie to Buchwald, Hartwig or others recorded; no recusal.
Aqvist: biomolecular simulation field is close to B032, which is shortlisted but not in his preferred configuration; he would note it if it became a serious contender.
Brzezinski and Zou are Stockholm University colleagues; neither candidate preference involves the other's work, and no recusal is apparent.
Aili: overlapping research with Sparr recorded in his profile; not judged a recusal issue.
No member discloses a conflict requiring recusal.
questions_for_round2: Does the committee regard Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling as conceptually distinct from the 2010 cross-coupling prize, and can the citation wording state this? Should Kosugi or Migita be named, or left to the citation?
For B026, is the committee willing to recognize the field before any PROTAC approval, and if so, is the third laureate Ciulli or Handa, or should a PROTAC and glue two-part structure be considered?

Is massively parallel sequencing, restricted to the Solexa chemistry and cluster readout, accepted as chemistry after the 1980 sequencing prize, and does the Balasubramanian and Klenerman pair settle the Mayer, Rothberg and Ju claims?

Should the prize be a single achievement or two parts, and if two parts, which pairs are compatible (for example B065 with B026, B037 or B045) given Somfai's and Aqvist's concern about two synthetic-methodology awards and the breadth of the prize?

For B045 and B056, can the record settle the allocation (Vancouver trio versus lipidoid line; which three of the perovskite pioneers), and do stability, toxicity and the 2023 Medicine prize alter timing?
Are there members who would move from their preferred configuration to a different ballot if the attribution or timing concerns above were resolved, and which resolution would change their ranking?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows no majority position. B065 has the most explicit preferences (three, with identical laureates), B026 has two with different third names, and B037, B045 and B056 each have one. Most members name B065 or B026 among their preferred or alternative choices, so the live questions are the 2010 overlap, the timing of B026 and the allocation within each candidate, rather than whether the underlying science is genuine. I have counted only explicit positions in the eight round-1 files and, as chair, give no ruling.
